content:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: *INC-3187* created by @Sean Gallagher — *Elevated tail latency (p99) in Hosted after runtime profile tweak*
Impact: Increased p99 latency on /v1/chat for subset of traffic
Status: Investigating
Owner: @Sean Gallagher
Links: dashboard https://grafana.redwood.dev/d/runtime-latency?var=route=chat | runbook https://confluence.redwood.dev/x/rollout-guardrails

Sean Gallagher: Seeing p99 jump starting ~10 min ago. p50/p95 mostly steady, p99 +70–120ms in us-east + eu-west. Error rate flat.
Looks correlated w/ today’s canary cohort that got profile pack default update.
Can someone from runtime join? I’m going to freeze further rollout.

Rafael Mendes: I’m here. I can pause the flag in Hosted. Which flag name are we using for profile pack? `runtime.profile_pack.enabled`?

Sean Gallagher: yep. Please pause at current canary size (don’t expand). Also confirm kill-switch semantics: does it revert to previous profile selection or disable pack entirely?

Rafael Mendes: kill-switch disables pack, falls back to legacy defaults (pre-1.22 selection). It does NOT automatically pin prior profile_version. Doing that separately if we want.
Pausing now.

Incident Bot: Deploy Bot: Feature flag `runtime.profile_pack.enabled` set to *HOLD* (no further cohort expansion). (requested by @Rafael Mendes)

Allison Grant: Looking at dashboard — p99 increase is mostly in `scheduler_queue_ms` (queueing) vs compute. GPU util not pegged, but queue depth spikes on mixed prompt lengths.
Also seeing a rise in `kernel_fallback_rate` on H100 canary pools (small but noticeable: 0.4% -> 2.1%).

Omar El-Sayed: I’m on. Any OOM/fragmentation signals? On-call bundle shows `kv_cache_fragmentation_est`?

Allison Grant: No OOM spikes. Fragmentation estimate slightly up but still below alert threshold. Compaction time increased a bit, but not huge.

Sean Gallagher: Confirmed impact scope: only canary pools (profile pack enabled) and H100 cohorts. L40S pools unaffected.
We need to decide: rollback canary to previous profile_version or disable profile pack entirely on canary.

Sofia Ivanova: Joining. The queueing increase + mixed prompt lengths sounds like the batching default we tweaked last week. Did we move max batch tokens or the prefill/decode prioritization weights in the new profile?

Lena Fischer: I can check the knob diff. The canary got profile `h100-prod-v1.0.3` (I think). That version increased `prefill_max_concurrency` and slightly raised `batching.target_tokens`.
If workload has lots of short prompts + some long contexts, it can starve long decode and inflate tail.

Hiro Tanaka: Kernel fallback rate up is concerning but maybe just correlated. If attention kernel v3 has stricter guards for long context it might fallback more and increase compute time, but Allison said it’s queueing.
Do we have p99 breakdown prefill vs decode?

Caleb Johnson: Traces show most of the delta in “time to first token” for requests that end up with longer decode. Prefill stage duration is ~flat. Queueing before prefill is +80ms at p99.
Compute time is basically unchanged.

Irene Choi: Infra note: us-east H100 canary pool includes a mix of SXM and PCIe instances (we’re mid-migration). If profile assumes a higher memory headroom or different scheduler params for SXM, it could behave worse on PCIe.
Do we tag by `sku_variant` anywhere?

Allison Grant: Not yet; only `sku=h100` label right now. I can slice by node pool name; the worst pool is `h100-us-east-3` which I believe is mostly PCIe.

Vanessa Ortiz: Confirming: `h100-us-east-3` is PCIe, driver minor is slightly behind baseline (still compatible but older). If selection logic didn’t catch that, we might be applying the newer profile to older driver.

Omar El-Sayed: That’s a big one — if profile selection is keyed on driver/CUDA and we have heterogeneity, it might choose an “unsafe” scheduler/memory set.
But you’d expect kernel fallbacks or weird allocator behavior. Queueing still points to scheduler/batching knobs.

Sean Gallagher: Immediate mitigation request: reduce impact now. Options:
1) Disable profile pack entirely for canary (revert to legacy).
2) Pin canary to previous profile_version (v1.0.2) while keeping pack for observability.
Which is safest / fastest?

Mateo Alvarez: I’m here. For mitigation, do (1) now to stop tail increase. Then we can do a controlled pin/test in a separate cohort.
We can re-enable pack w/ explicit pin once we identify the knob.

Rafael Mendes: I can flip kill-switch for canary cohort only (targeted) if we have cohort config. Otherwise it’s global flag.
Right now pack is enabled only for canary pools, so disabling globally should just turn it off for that canary.
Confirm ok?

Sean Gallagher: ok proceed w/ disable. We can re-enable later behind pin.

Incident Bot: Deploy Bot: Feature flag `runtime.profile_pack.enabled` set to *OFF* for Hosted (canary-only exposure). (requested by @Rafael Mendes)

Allison Grant: Watching dashboards — queue depth already trending down. p99 is starting to recover but still elevated (needs a few minutes for traffic to drain).
Kernel fallback rate returning to baseline too.

Sofia Ivanova: For RCA, I want the exact knob diff between `h100-prod-v1.0.2` and `v1.0.3`. Likely `batching.max_prefill_tokens` or queue limits.
Lena, can you paste the relevant snippet?

Lena Fischer: From my notes (not 100% until I confirm in repo):
- `scheduler.workload_buckets.enabled=true` (already)
- `scheduler.queue_limit_requests`: 640 -> 800
- `batching.target_tokens`: 2048 -> 3072
- `prefill_decode_fairness`: 0.55 -> 0.62 (more prefill priority)
That last change can absolutely hurt long decode tails under mixed load.

Hiro Tanaka: On kernel side, v3 fallback guard changed for long context windows > 16k, but that’s only a small fraction. I’ll keep an eye but I think scheduler is main culprit.

Vanessa Ortiz: If we’re doing follow-up test, please ensure we only test on homogeneous pool (SXM only) to remove PCIe variance, and pick a pool at baseline driver.

Omar El-Sayed: +1, and we should add logging in startup summary to show detected driver + selected profile_id/profile_version (I know that’s landing in 1.22 but not sure everywhere yet).

Sean Gallagher: Current status: mitigation applied (pack off). Monitoring for full recovery for 15 mins. If stable, we can resolve incident and open follow-up tasks.
Action items:
- Runtime: confirm knob diff + propose fix (likely revert fairness or lower batching) (@Sofia Ivanova, @Lena Fischer)
- Observability: add `sku_variant` / driver tag or pool metadata to dashboards (@Allison Grant, @Caleb Johnson)
- Infra: validate driver heterogeneity in canary pools + advise selection guardrails (@Vanessa Ortiz, @Irene Choi)

Allison Grant: p99 back within 5% of baseline now. scheduler_queue_ms p99 normalized.

Mateo Alvarez: Please link this incident in the PR/issue for the batching default. We should also update the rollout gates to explicitly watch `scheduler_queue_ms` and TTFT p99 for mixed workloads.

Rafael Mendes: Do we want to re-enable pack with pin to v1.0.2 for canary after things cool down? Or wait for fix?

Sean Gallagher: Wait for fix. Let’s keep pack off until we have a revert in place + canary plan.
I’ll mark incident as mitigated once stable for 10 more mins.

Incident Bot: Status update by @Sean Gallagher: *Mitigated* — profile pack disabled for Hosted canary; latency recovered. Continuing monitoring.

Sofia Ivanova: I’ll open a follow-up: revert `prefill_decode_fairness` change and reduce target_tokens for v1.0.4, then rerun benchmark matrix bucket “mixed-short-long”.

Omar El-Sayed: I’ll also add a note to expected behavior doc: “If queue_ms rises while compute stays flat, suspect scheduling/batching knobs; rollback profile_version / disable pack.”

Sean Gallagher: Closing soon if stable. Thanks all.

Incident Bot: :white_check_mark: *INC-3187 resolved* by @Sean Gallagher
Resolution: Disabled profile pack in Hosted canary; restored baseline tail latency. Follow-ups filed for profile knob adjustment + improved tags/guardrails.
